business_rules.statement: A scheduled obligation not in the deployable register does not exist and must not be deployed; a timer discovered running in production without a register row is disabled on discovery.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Deployment-time reconciliation between declared definitions and registered ones

business_rules.statement: A state not already present in the four state registers is a scope decision, not an implementation detail.
business_rules.applies_to: Occurrence, command, capture and notification states

business_rules.statement: The registers are re-linted; a blank cell fails the build.
Every deployed scheduled definition appears in the register with no blank column.
No definition of authority class A uses mechanism class M8, M9, M10 or M11 as primary.
No state outside the four registers appears in any code path or user interface string.
Every adapter has two working implementations under contract test.
Every FB-SCHED-* carries the full canon field set.
All fifteen diagrams exist and each names the register or state set it renders.
Every state machine rendered matches its register exactly.
business_rules.applies_to: State machine diagrams D3, D6, D7, D8

business_rules.statement: All ten cards are present, each with source references, ambiguity, options, recommendation, trade-offs, product, role, security, offline, AI and implementation impacts, and a decision owner.
business_rules.enforcement_point: TEST-SCHED-377-01 card-completeness lint over the twelve required fields

business_rules.statement: Every scheduled-work definition references either `settled` or an open `DEC-SCHED-*` card.
Every inherited contradiction this chapter touches is referenced by identifier with both readings preserved and neither silently resolved.
Every numbered finding in section 45A.2 appears exactly once in this crosswalk.
No artefact derived from this chapter claims completeness while any `DEC-SCHED-*` card is open.
Every canonical obligation in 45A.17.1 is reachable from this crosswalk, from a numbered finding or from the independent-provenance table.
No obligation is deployed under an identifier absent from section 45A.17.1.
Every finding classified as not a scheduled obligation states the mechanism that carries the behaviour instead.

THE CLOSING STATEMENT: No completeness claim can be made for the scheduled-work architecture of AVIIXA while any of DEC-SCHED-001 through DEC-SCHED-010 remains open. Ten are open at the time of writing.
An occurrence blocked by a legal hold or a suspension is rendered as visibly overdue and never folded into the succeeded count; none of the occurrence states may be collapsed into 'done'.
'Synced' is never a state in the capture state register.
Sending is not delivery; delivery is not opening; opening is not acknowledgement; acknowledgement is not the business action.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Notification state register and D8 state machine

business_rules.statement: Where 45A.17.1 and 45A.17.2 differ from narrative chapters 27 and 30A short forms, the deployable register and crosswalk are authoritative and the narrative is illustrative.

Cross-tenant data isolation is platform-fixed for everyone always; cross-tenant analytics anonymisation is ENFORCED, locked in Super Admin settings with no off position for any account including the root.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Authorization predicate on every data path; aggregation pipeline locked in Settings

business_rules.statement: No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console. Layer 3 record-level content is reached only through an audited, session-scoped access under one of the three named access classes.
Absent an open access-class session, a layer-3 request is refused — not filtered to an empty set, refused — so the refusal is auditable.
No console view that compares tenants renders any tenant identifier, and no account including the root can disable that behaviour.
Any attempt to read record-level operational content without an open, in-date access-class session is refused, and the refusal writes an audit event.
Every platform-side access event against a tenant appears in that tenant's Platform Access History and audit log, from the moment the session opens.
A work package delivered to a Frontline device contains only the data its assigned runs require.
A data-access path constructed without a tenant predicate fails closed in a test harness rather than returning rows.

Authorization is a fixed-order twelve-step gauntlet: authenticate; resolve roles and three scopes additively; read current object state from the record of truth; tenant predicate; role rule; scope rule; object-state rule; segregation of duties; field-level annotations; route privileged actions into approval; commit action and audit in one transaction; enqueue device commands with honest states.

Separation of duties is creator != approver, satisfied by any second holder of the approving role; it appears at the Job state machine, the Studio chain Author→Reviewer→Release Authority, the console maker-checker cycle, and the compliance-emergency path.
business_rules.applies_to: Jobs, publications, platform changes, emergency access

business_rules.statement: The creator of a Job cannot approve that Job, and the refusal names the rule rather than showing a generic error.
Lot release is offered only to Quality Managers on every surface, with no work-type, risk-class or tag exception.
business_rules.enforcement_point: TEST-SEC-202 across every surface and API path

business_rules.statement: The audit log records identity and action and never records an acting-as-role attribution.
A tenant always has at least one Tenant Admin, and an approver-capable role holder exists whenever a Job exists; the platform refuses the removal that would break either rule.
Every authorization decision reads the object's current state; no decision is made against a cached projection.
The Read-only Auditor has no Client Command Center access on any path.

The login is the credential, not the device: identity, qualifications, language preference and attribution travel with the worker onto any conformant device; a shared tablet confers nothing by itself.
There is no self-registration, no password-only path, and no role-escalation path on the console except the root acting.
A second-identity step-up captures the authorising identity against exactly one authorisation and does not alter or end the worker's session.
A sync is forced before a sign-off; where the device is offline the sign-off is refused and stated as refused, never queued as if completed.
Logging in on an unexpected device succeeds and raises an audit flag; no hard block exists at V1.
Personal-identification-number lockout occurs after repeated failures and is reset only through the managed-credential path owned by the Delivery Operations Hub.
The offline trust window extends the life of an answer the server already gave; it never creates an answer the server has not given.
A tenant may shorten the offline credential-trust window and may never set it above 72 hours; an out-of-bound value is rejected at entry with the bound stated, never accepted and logged.
After the window expires with no sync, the device refuses new run starts and states the reason in the worker's language.
No offline path grants a qualification clearance, performs a sign-off, or releases a lot hold.
A device timestamp outside the tenant's clock-skew threshold is not trusted to order writes; the event routes to human resolution.
No Frontline screen states or implies that an offline device has received or applied a command.
Every remote wipe attempts a final sync of pending captures before any erasure.
Wipe and de-authorisation cannot be executed without root approval and are mirrored to the tenant's audit stream.
No surface shows a device as wiped while the wipe command has not been applied and acknowledged.
Captured media exists only inside the application's encrypted store and never in the device gallery or any shared operating-system location.
business_rules.enforcement_point: TEST-SEC-503 gallery probe on Android and iOS

business_rules.statement: On a compliance suspension the application locks at next contact, preserves all local data, and shows the fixed message verbatim in the worker's language.
Media is evicted from a device only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check.
Encryption at rest and encryption in transit render locked with the ENFORCED badge, with no control and no approval path, for every account including the root.
An attempt to change a locked setting produces an audit event of the locked-setting-attempt class.
No interface anywhere presents tamper-evident audit as an available V1 capability.
If DEC-SEC-015 adopts package signing, a package failing verification is quarantined, never used, and never silently replaced.
An action that cannot be audited does not happen: the audit entry commits in the same transaction as the action it records; both commit or neither does.
business_rules.applies_to: Every consequential action on every surface

business_rules.statement: No surface, role or administrative path offers delete or edit on any audit entry, including the root account.
Where the audit event cannot be written, the business change does not commit, and the user is told the action did not take place.
Every reclassification, correction or annotation is a new append-only entry; the original entry remains readable.
Exactly three platform access classes exist; no fourth path into tenant record-level content is reachable from any console screen or API.
No write operation is possible inside a normal support session, on any path.
A compliance-emergency session opens only with a named emergency class, a declared scope, and two distinct human authorisations — the root and one Admin.
The tenant's End-session control terminates a support session immediately and the termination is audited.
No platform operator ever acts under a tenant user's identity; every action names the operator.
JBS holds no standing access; every JBS grant is scoped, time-boxed, reason-linked and expires.
No path on any surface purges operational data; shortening a retention horizon changes storage tier only.
Anonymisation never executes for a tenant in Regulated-Industry mode.
Anonymisation preserves the measurement, the result and the evidence, and replaces identity with an opaque worker identifier.
Upcoming anonymisation and tiering events surface before they execute.
A legal hold suspends tiering and compliance-driven deletion for its declared scope, and its placement and release are dual-approved and tenant-visible.
Retention-horizon changes require root approval and write to both audit trails.
No interface claims General Data Protection Regulation compliance at V1.
Anonymisation is the lifecycle's one irreversible act: switching a tenant into Regulated mode later cannot resurrect identities already anonymised.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Data lifecycle state machine — no edge out of Anonymised

business_rules.statement: A successful prompt injection cannot cause a missed deviation, cannot release a Severity 1 hold, cannot alter a specification limit, and cannot bypass a gate; the bound is architectural.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Deterministic on-device detection layer with no AI in the triggering path

business_rules.statement: No artificial-intelligence component participates in deviation triggering, severity classification, or gate evaluation on any surface.
Agent-originated proposals are validated against the tenant-configuration registry bounds before they are displayed for human decision.
Tenant-originated content entering model context is structurally marked as data, and no instruction within it is followed.
Nothing from one tenant's memory stores appears in another tenant's agent context, and no tenant data becomes external training data.
The emergency pause renders as explicit agent unavailability and never suppresses the on-device deterministic layer.
Every scheduled execution runs under a named service identity, and no audit entry attributes a scheduled action to a human who did not perform it.
Every scheduled execution authorises against current state at execution time; a schedule whose authority has been revoked does not execute.
A duplicate occurrence has no effect and is recorded as a suppressed duplicate.
A command already applied by a device is rejected on re-delivery, and a command whose precondition no longer holds is rejected rather than applied.
Schedule creation, change, replay, backfill, pause, resume, cancellation and override are approvable objects; none applies silently.
Replay and backfill capture a mandatory justification and display the blast radius before approval.
Occurrences produced by a backfill are flagged as backfilled wherever they appear.
business_rules.enforcement_point: TEST-SEC-1107 backfill labelling in both audit streams

business_rules.statement: The run auto-close scheduler performs the platform's only automatic state transition and no other.
Every critical-class action requires root approval and cannot be applied by its proposer.
business_rules.enforcement_point: TEST-SEC-1201 self-approval probe, TEST-SEC-1202 critical-class routing

business_rules.statement: A Platform Engineer's mutating change never applies directly; it submits into the approval cycle.
Console user creation and role changes are performed only by the root account.
A change awaiting approval is visibly pending on the object and in the queue; nothing applies silently.
No console screen shows a device-affecting privileged action as in force before the device has acknowledged it.
No incident-response action bypasses tenant isolation, the audit guarantee, or the access-class requirement for record-level content.
An in-app incident banner cannot be muted and displays for its defined duration.
Personal-device enrollment is not offered until DEC-SEC-025 is resolved.
Every §7.11 position is implemented regardless of whether its detail has landed.
No section of Chapter 46 claims complete coverage while an open decision remains.

The Statement of Work gives no service-level agreement, no Recovery Time Objective, no Recovery Point Objective, no concurrency figure, no throughput figure, no device count, no tenant count and no latency target; each is a contractual value this blueprint may not invent.

decisions.question: The scheduled-work mechanism baseline — what actually holds a deadline?
options: (a) The full recommended baseline of 45A.9.4
(b) Relational scheduler only, with no managed trigger, no queue and no workflow engine
(c) Provider-native scheduling throughout, accepting lock-in
decisions.impact: Determines the adapter implementations built first; no tenant-visible product impact

decisions.question: Durable workflow engine at V1, or deferred?
options: (a) Adopt a durable workflow engine for the named bounded set
(b) Implement the same obligations in the relational scheduler with hand-written state
(c) Adopt an engine for gate escalation only, as a pilot
decisions.impact: Determines whether BusinessDeadline has one implementation or two at V1

decisions.question: Customer-hosted deployment parity — must a customer-hosted deployment ever be supported?
options: (a) Commit to parity now and build both implementations of all five adapters
(b) Commit to cloud only and accept provider coupling
(c) Commit to parity for the authority layer only
decisions.impact: Determines adapter test scope

decisions.question: Provider selection and the cost envelope — no provider named beyond 'cloud' and no cost envelope exists.
options: (a) Name a provider now and optimise for its managed services
(b) Stay provider-neutral and accept a small efficiency cost
(c) Name a provider for V1 with a documented exit cost
decisions.impact: Large implementation impact, confined to adapters; sets platform-team training

decisions.question: Scheduler visibility surfaces — how is the scheduler seen and operated?
options: (a) Full Scheduler Registry and Occurrence Detail screens plus Client Command Center overdue strip
(b) Settings-only, with no registry screen
(c) Registry screen for the platform team, nothing tenant-facing
decisions.impact: Determines whether the Client Command Center gains a scheduled-obligation strip; two to three screens

decisions.question: Recovery objectives, intervals and tolerances — every operational number in the chapter is undefined by the source.
options: (a) Fixed absolute values per definition
(b) Multiples of each definition's own cadence
(c) Service-level objectives with error budgets for the four highest-consequence definitions and cadence multiples for the rest
decisions.impact: Determines tenant-facing timeliness promises and on-call burden; configuration not architecture

decisions.question: Retry limits, dead-letter policy and command validity — every bounded-retry value is unspecified.
options: (a) One limit for everything
(b) Limits varying by authority class
(c) Limits varying by authority class plus a maximum event age
decisions.impact: Governs what happens to a device returning after a long absence; command validity is a security control

decisions.question: Retention alignment for scheduler-owned stores (workflow engine, queue, metrics store).
options: (a) Align every scheduler-owned store to the platform's retention model
(b) Treat scheduler stores as transient and keep references only, with short retention
(c) Case by case
decisions.impact: Substantial security impact — option (b) is why a compromised queue cannot exfiltrate captures

decisions.question: Measurement, privacy and aggregate suppression — no minimum-population value, no employment-data policy.
options: (a) No individual measurement at V1 and none on the roadmap
(b) No individual measurement at V1, with a defined process for a future request
(c) Individual measurement permitted with consent and controls
decisions.impact: Determines what the Custom Report Builder may cut by and what a Supervisor may see on drill

decisions.question: Operational ownership, paging and the observability stack.
options: (a) The client's platform team owns everything, with JBS on a granted, time-boxed basis
(b) JBS operates under a standing grant
(c) A shared rotation with defined handover
decisions.impact: Defines who is paged for each ALRT-SCHED-*; runbooks, rotations, observability product

decisions.question: Absence of a crosswalk between the numbered discovery register and the mnemonic deployable register.
options: publish the crosswalk
decisions.adopted_working_position: Closed by the crosswalk published at section 45A.17.2
decisions.impact: Resolves every numbered finding to a canonical obligation or a not-an-obligation classification

decisions.question: Physical tenant-isolation topology — shared schema with a discriminator, schema-per-tenant, or database-per-tenant?
options: shared schema with tenant discriminator
schema-per-tenant
database-per-tenant
decisions.impact: Cost and compliance decision; isolation enforcement design

decisions.question: The list of fields treated as personal data for field-level permission.
options: declarative annotation on the data model (recommended)
per-screen logic
decisions.impact: Determines who can see a worker's name; slows Custom Report Builder data-set work

decisions.question: Multi-factor requirement for tenant Quality Managers — refuse a session whose assertion reports no second factor?
options: inherit only
record and display
enforce
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: record and display at V1; enforce as a tenant setting later
decisions.impact: Enforcement depends on assertion fidelity the platform does not control

decisions.question: Console session timeout value.
options: 15 minutes idle
30 minutes idle
60 minutes idle
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: 30 minutes idle with re-authentication, 8 hours absolute
decisions.impact: Shorter timeouts interrupt long approval reviews

decisions.question: Personal-identification-number length.
options: 4 digits
6 digits
8 digits
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: 6 digits with a banned-sequence list
decisions.impact: 6 digits is measurably slower than 4 in glove testing

decisions.question: Personal-identification-number lockout threshold and duration.
options: 3 / 5 / 10 attempts
lockout 5 minutes
lockout until supervisor reset
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: 5 attempts, then lockout until reset via the managed-credential path
decisions.impact: A hard lock stops a worker mid-shift and needs a supervisor present

decisions.question: Reauthentication interval for privileged tenant actions.
options: none
per action
per 15 minutes
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: fresh proof for lot release and Job approval
decisions.impact: Adds friction to the two actions quality auditors care most about

decisions.question: Trust-window expiry warning lead time.
options: warn at 25 per cent remaining and again at 10 per cent, visually only
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation — R&D: 25 per cent then 10 per cent, visual only
decisions.impact: Two more on-screen states to author, translate and test

decisions.question: Behaviour of a run under way at the exact moment of trust-window expiry.
options: run under way continues to completion and submission; no new run may start
strict stop at expiry
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommended default: continue the run under way; no new run may start
decisions.impact: Extends maximum trusted-credential age by one run beyond the configured window

decisions.question: Key hierarchy, custody, rotation, and customer-managed keys.
options: envelope encryption with per-tenant DEK wrapped by a platform KEK in a managed key service
bring-your-own-key for tenants
no value proposed for rotation periods
decisions.impact: Enables cryptographic erasure; complicates cross-tenant anonymised analytics

decisions.question: Work-package signing at V1 or later.
options: sign at publication with device-side verification and quarantine at V1
defer as a later hardening alongside audit tamper-evidence
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation — R&D: sign packages and the versioned severity-classification table; quarantine on failure
decisions.impact: Without it a device-side alteration of specification limits is undetectable — the largest V1 cryptographic gap

decisions.question: Model and prompt artifact digests — refuse to load an artifact whose digest does not match the evaluation-gated one?
options: record and verify digests, refuse to load on mismatch
no artifact integrity control
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation — R&D: verify digests at load
decisions.impact: Without it the artifact that passed evaluation and the artifact that runs may differ

decisions.question: Compliance-emergency session default time box (the two-hour default belongs to normal support sessions only).
options: a named default value
decisions.impact: Bounds break-glass write access into tenant data

decisions.question: Evidence-media personal-data position — automated redaction of evidence media?
options: do not attempt automated redaction at V1; state the position and put capture guidance into Studio authoring
attempt automated redaction
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation — R&D: no automated redaction at V1
decisions.impact: Places a duty on tenant authors; harder once European data protection enters scope

decisions.question: Whether a legal hold suspends anonymisation (the source states it suspends tiering and compliance-driven deletion only).
options: legal hold suspends anonymisation
legal hold does not suspend anonymisation
decisions.impact: A hold that does not stop anonymisation could destroy the attribution the hold exists to preserve

decisions.question: Access class required for the Trace Viewer — traces are platform-internal but may contain tenant operational content.
options: trace access sits behind an access class as layer-3 content
console module with no access-class qualification
decisions.adopted_working_position: Derived Clarification: trace access is layer-3 content and must sit behind an access class
decisions.impact: Otherwise the trace viewer becomes the ambient-browsing path the source forbids

decisions.question: Anchoring the trust window to server-observed time at last sync rather than to device time.
options: anchor to server-observed time
keep device-time anchoring
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation — R&D: anchor to server-observed time at last sync
decisions.impact: A device clock set backward could otherwise extend apparent trust

decisions.question: Security-incident severity scheme.
options: adopt the proposed four (A/B/C/D)
align to the client's existing corporate scheme
align to the SOC 2 framework's incident taxonomy
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: align to the client's corporate scheme if one exists
decisions.impact: Notification deadlines attach to these definitions

decisions.question: Pre-authorised containment during a declared incident — may a named incident commander pause agents and revoke grants without critical-class approval?
options: standing narrow pre-authorisation with root notified and review within a stated period
no pre-authorisation
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation — R&D: define a narrowly scoped, time-limited, heavily audited pre-authorisation
decisions.impact: Every containment lever is currently critical-class or root-only — a response-time hazard

decisions.question: Tenant notification deadline after confirmed exposure, and breach-notification obligations.
options: a stated deadline per severity
decisions.impact: Contractual value; interacts with DEC-CERT-001 and deferred GDPR alignment

decisions.question: Application-scoped wipe on a personal device, and whether personal devices may be enrolled at all.
options: wipe confined to the application's own store (blueprint reading)
broader wipe
no personal-device enrollment
decisions.adopted_working_position: Derived Clarification: a wipe can only reach the application's own data — read as application-scoped throughout
decisions.impact: Blocks personal-device enrollment until resolved

decisions.question: Immutability claim versus deferred tamper-evidence — can an immutability claim that cannot be independently verified stand at V1?
options: Reading A: append-only application semantics plus infrastructure controls satisfy the immutability claim at V1 (§8.18)
Reading B: an unverifiable immutability claim is a control gap the §4.10.2 deferral acknowledges
decisions.adopted_working_position: This blueprint does not choose; both readings preserved
decisions.impact: An external auditor asking 'prove this log was not edited' cannot be answered at V1

decisions.question: Is the onboarding authoring role a fourth write path into tenant data, contradicting §8.15.2's 'only one' claim?
options: Reading A: a tenant-granted role held by a platform-side person, therefore tenant-side access
Reading B: a fourth write path needing an exception clause or a fourth named class
decisions.impact: Leaves one write path into tenant data unresolved

decisions.question: Whether an impersonation capability exists (the single §4.12.4 mention of 'cross-tenant visibility and impersonation control').
options: Reading: no user impersonation at V1 — the mention is control over cross-tenant visibility
Reading: an impersonation feature exists
decisions.adopted_working_position: Derived Clarification: this blueprint reads V1 as having no user impersonation
decisions.impact: If impersonation exists, every audit attribution becomes ambiguous

decisions.question: Wipe reaching an offline device: how long may a wipe command remain pending, and what if the device never returns?
options: Reading A: final-sync attempt is a precondition — a device that never reconnects is never wiped, the command remains pending indefinitely
Reading B: final-sync attempt is best-effort — a device reconnecting after a stated period wipes without the sync succeeding
decisions.status: Carried from canon — unresolved, both readings preserved
decisions.impact: Reading A leaves data on a stolen device forever; reading B may discard unsynced captures

decisions.question: Capture-upload versus command-download ordering at reconnect.
options: safety: commands first so a suspension, wipe or hold lands before more work
data integrity: captures first so no unsynced evidence is risked
decisions.adopted_working_position: Adopted 2026-08-14: stop-class commands apply first, then the full capture queue uploads, then enabling-class commands apply
decisions.status: adopted working position — awaiting client ratification
decisions.impact: Fixes reconnection ordering across all offline devices; both source readings preserved in the card

decisions.question: Action-agent gating — does the Prevention Agent's pre-authorised policy constitute a gate?
options: pre-authorised policy is a gate
pre-authorised policy is not a gate
decisions.adopted_working_position: Adopted 2026-08-14: gating is declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field; the Prevention Agent is bound to `authoring-time policy`
decisions.impact: Determines which agent effects require a runtime human gate

decisions.question: Soft suspension exit.
decisions.adopted_working_position: Adopted as a binding working position on 2026-08-14, source contradiction kept on the record
decisions.status: adopted working position — awaiting client ratification
decisions.impact: Governs SCHED-SUSPEND-SOFT behaviour

decisions.question: Storage-full behaviour on a Frontline device.
decisions.status: Carried from canon — explicitly deferred to the Frontline Functional Specification
decisions.impact: Determines whether a full device can be made to drop evidence

decisions.question: Meaning of `Supervisor+` and `QM+` across five additive, non-hierarchical roles.
options: 'the named role or any role explicitly granted that action' (this chapter's reading)
an ordering across roles
decisions.adopted_working_position: This chapter reads them as 'the named role or any role explicitly granted that action', preserving both readings
decisions.impact: Invites an implementation that infers a hierarchy — privilege-escalation risk RISK-SEC-02

decisions.question: Plant Manager and Quality Director — do they exist as roles?

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The authorization service degrades (role store unreachable, current state unreadable, SoD history unavailable, audit writer down)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Deny the specific action and state the failing stage in plain language
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Surface degrades to read-only for the affected object class, then read-only entirely
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Tenant web surfaces read-only; the floor continues to execute and capture offline; nothing lost, nothing approved
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Three consecutive self-test passes and a drained audit queue; a reconciliation report lists every refused action

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The identity provider is unreachable (outage, assertion clock skew, certificate expiry, managed-credential store unavailable)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Staff holding a managed credential use the managed-credential path
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The surface refuses new sessions and says so plainly; it does not open a reduced-privilege anonymous mode
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No new sessions; existing sessions expire naturally; devices continue within the trust window then stop accepting new work
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Provider health restored and two successful synthetic logins; deferred forced-sync actions re-offered rather than silently skipped

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The trust window expires with no coverage (site-wide loss, shielded area, manipulated device clock)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The worker walks the device into coverage; the connectivity-loss protocol is already running
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Supervisor reassigns affected runs to a device in coverage; then the site falls back to paper or a deterministic manual procedure
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The device accepts no new runs, holds all committed captures durably, and displays the lapsed message
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A successful sync; on reconnection commands and captures exchange in the DEC-SYNC-001 order; late captures fold in flagged late_arrival

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A device is lost with unsynced work
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Leave the wipe command pending and rely on the encrypted store (reading A of DEC-WIPE-001)
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the client decides a pending wipe expires into an unconditional erase, lost captures are recorded as explicit audited data loss with affected runs listed — never a silent gap
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Wipe command remains pending and visible; device data remains encrypted at rest; affected runs remain open until the finish window closes
failures_fallbacks.recovery: If the device returns, final sync uploads captures which fold in flagged late_arrival; otherwise the audited-recompute rule governs

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Key material unavailable or suspected compromised
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry against a replica of the key service; serve from a protected short-lived decrypted working set
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Rotate the affected key version and re-wrap; where re-wrap cannot complete, declare an incident naming the affected scope
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform withholds the affected data and says so — withholding is correct, degrading to plaintext is not
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Key service restored and a successful decrypt canary across every affected data class; undecryptable records listed as integrity exceptions

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The audit writer is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The transaction fails and the user is told the action did not occur
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Mutating operations suspended platform-wide while read paths continue; then the platform enters a read-only terminal state
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Platform read-only; floor continues and queues; nothing approved, released, cleared, published or configured
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Audit store healthy and a synthetic audited action committing; reconciliation compares operational state against the audit stream for the outage window

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A session cannot be closed or its mirroring fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Hard server-side expiry independent of the expiry job; the session token is short-lived and cannot be extended without fresh authorisation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where mirroring cannot be written the session is refused rather than opened; during a genuine emergency mirroring is queued durably or an incident is declared
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No platform-side access into tenant context is possible; the tenant is unaffected operationally
failures_fallbacks.recovery: All sessions closed and the mirroring queue drained; any session with unmirrored actions is reported to the tenant explicitly

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The anonymisation or tiering scheduler misbehaves (wrong tenant posture, legal hold in force, fails to run, wrong tiering)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The scheduler refuses to execute any batch whose pre-flight check disagrees with the tenant-configuration registry and raises the disagreement as an incident
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Platform-wide scheduler halt — data ages but nothing moves and nothing anonymises
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Schedulers halted, data intact, tenants informed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Deferred batches run with pre-flight checks; any record anonymised in error is recorded as an irreversible incident, never as a corrected one

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Agent output is untrustworthy or the model layer fails (suspected injection, model unavailability, runaway loops, drift, poisoned corpus)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Router failover to the fallback model role
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Emergency pause checkpoints in-flight agent runs at their next stage boundary; agents remain paused indefinitely
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A fully deterministic platform with no agent assistance, honestly labelled — a degraded product, not an unsafe one
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Cause resolved, evaluation gate re-passed, resume approved as its own critical-class act; parked runs continue from checkpoints; pre-pause proposals re-validated against current bounds

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A scheduler misfires, duplicates, or executes on stale authority
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refuse the occurrence and alert — a skipped occurrence is recoverable through an approved backfill; a wrongly executed anonymisation is not
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Pause the affected scheduler as an audited act; then a platform-wide scheduler halt
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Schedulers halted with an explicit list of every deferred occurrence, visible to the platform team and affected tenants
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Every deferred occurrence enumerated and either backfilled with approval, or formally abandoned with a recorded reason

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The approval queue is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Proposals are refused rather than auto-applied
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: All mutating administrative change stops platform-wide; tenant-side approval chains are separate and unaffected
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform's configuration is frozen at its last approved state
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Queue healthy and a synthetic approval round-trip; applied changes compared against approval records — any applied change without an approval record is a control incident

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A registered threat is realised
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The incident-response model in 46.14
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The register row is revisited before the incident is closed and its residual-risk sentence rewritten
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Controlled hold — devices continue enforcing specification gates locally; mutating administrative change stops until integrity is re-established
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Every control named in the affected row is re-tested, not merely inspected

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Incident response itself fails (root unreachable, announcement console affected, alerting missed it, commander unavailable)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The deputy incident commander, named in advance
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Out-of-band contact with the root custodian; absent DEC-SEC-023 there is no platform-side substitute
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Affected tenants informed, containment pending, the incident visibly open — an unsatisfactory state, stated plainly
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On containment, reconcile per the affected fallback contract, then review

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The deep security pass does not land before build
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Implement to the strongest defensible interpretation of each stated position and record it as an Assumption requiring confirmation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Implement key handling using cloud-provider managed key service defaults, recorded as provisional; personal devices are not enrolled until the position lands
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Shared, tenant-owned devices only; encryption at provider defaults; wipe implemented as reading A of DEC-WIPE-001
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On delivery, re-specify affected acceptance criteria and tests and rewrite affected threat-register rows

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Cross-tenant data leakage via a data path missing its tenant predicate or a comparative view rendering identifiers
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Isolation platform-fixed §1.5; analytics anonymisation ENFORCED §8.7.4; three-layer model with no ambient browsing §8.1.2
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A defect inside the enforcement layer is not caught by the enforcement layer
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Continuous independent cross-tenant probe running as a synthetic tenant, alerting on any foreign row

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Privilege escalation within a tenant via accumulating additive role grants or a defect treating `Supervisor+` as an ordering
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Five fixed roles; additive multi-role with identity-based audit; segregation of duties; Command Center action set closed at ten
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: DEC-PLUS-001 leaves `Supervisor+` and `QM+` undefined, inviting an implementation that infers a hierarchy
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resolve DEC-PLUS-001 before implementation; add a periodic effective-permission report per user for the Tenant Admin

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Compromised root account via credential theft against the single root account
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Exactly one root, backend-created; SSO, MFA, allowlist, short sessions; invariants bind the root; every root action audited
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A single account is a single point of catastrophic compromise and the only account that can create accounts
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Hardware-bound authentication for the root; a documented custody and recovery procedure held by the client; alerting on every root authentication

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Compromised device altering the work package's specification limits or severity mappings
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Application-managed encrypted store; minimal on-device scope; media confined to the application; version pinning
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Nothing in the source verifies the integrity of the package the device executes; an altered limit produces silence, not an error
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Package signing with device-side verification and quarantine (DEC-SEC-015); a device-integrity signal reported as fleet telemetry

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Lost or stolen tablet; offline extraction of the application store
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Encrypted store; wipe with final sync; login is the credential so the device confers no authority; eviction only after confirmed receipt
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: DEC-WIPE-001 leaves an unreachable device's wipe unresolved; extraction remains possible with sufficient capability
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resolve DEC-WIPE-001; bind the store key to device-held key material (DEC-SEC-014)

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Package or model tampering — substituting artifacts between publication and execution
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Evaluation gate hard for every operator; sandbox-before-publish ENFORCED; semantic versioning with author classification and reviewer validation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Versioning proves intent, not integrity; the artifact that passed evaluation and the artifact that runs may differ undetectably
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Artifact digests verified at load (DEC-SEC-016); signed packages (DEC-SEC-015)

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Insider misusing support access — many small, individually plausible sessions
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Support read-only without exception; ticket-linked reason and time box; tenant banner with End-session; mirroring; no ambient browsing
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Nothing in the source detects a pattern of many small sessions
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Per-engineer session-rate and breadth analytics with an alert threshold, surfaced to the tenant as well as the platform

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Malicious or careless integration writing bad data or exhausting capacity
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Integration Surface is a tenant-side module; ERP/MES connectors scaffolded only at V1; outbound webhooks deferred
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The scaffolded stub endpoint is a live surface even if unactivated; no rate limit, quota or validation posture is stated
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Treat the stub endpoint as a hostile input boundary from day one: schema validation, per-tenant quota, and back-pressure

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Prompt injection through evidence, free text or an uploaded document
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: No model in the deviation-triggering path; on-device classification; human gate or pre-authorised policy; the platform never invents content, rules or thresholds
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Agent output can still mislead a human decision-maker; no injection control is specified
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Untrusted-region marking, capability minimisation, registry-bound validation at the sink

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Poisoned coaching corpus — content inserted to be retrieved and shown to workers
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Studio approval chain for content; nothing becomes external training data; coaching renders from authored variants
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The corpus index is rebuilt from assets whose approval state is not verified at rebuild time in any stated control
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Rebuild the corpus only from approved, versioned assets, and audit rebuilds as publications

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Audit suppression by an insider with infrastructure access manipulating the audit store beneath the application
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Append-only with no delete or edit path on any surface; one-transaction guarantee ENFORCED; no purge
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Tamper-evidence is deferred beyond V1, so suppression beneath the application is not detectable by the platform
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Write-once storage semantics; continuous class-filtered export to a separately credentialed location; periodic external digest (DEC-AUDIT-001)

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Replay of a stale command — re-delivering a previously applied or now-invalid command
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Commands recorded centrally and applied in order at the device's next sync; pull-based command channel; five command classes only
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No anti-replay control is specified anywhere; a replayed lot-release command is a safety event
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Idempotency keys per occurrence, device-side applied-command records, and precondition validation at apply time — the highest-value addition in the register

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Clock manipulation on a device — setting the device clock forward or backward
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Clock-skew threshold default ~5 minutes, ceiling 60; out-of-threshold timestamps not trusted to order writes and routed to human resolution; skew events as fleet telemetry
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The skew guard protects ordering; it is not stated to protect the trust window, so a clock set backward could extend apparent trust
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Anchor the trust window to server-observed time at last sync; alert on repeated threshold breaches (DEC-SEC-021)

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Denial of service against the sync endpoint or the command-pull path
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Offline-first architecture; connectivity-loss protocol at 30, 60 and 120 minutes; the deterministic layer is local
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No rate limit, quota, concurrency figure or throughput figure is stated anywhere in the source
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Per-device and per-tenant rate limiting with exponential backoff and jitter; a durable device queue so rejection costs nothing (DEC-NFR-003)

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A surface implies an offline device acted
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Fifteen-state command model, rendering tests, AC-SCHED-190
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Severe — the platform's core honesty claim
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Residual Low

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Duplicate execution writes a second official record
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Business-outcome idempotency keys, unique constraints
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Severe; High likelihood without controls
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Residual Low

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A missed safety obligation is never noticed
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Absence alerting, ALRT-SCHED-01
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Severe
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Residual Low

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Anonymisation runs wrongly
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Mode check, hold check, dry run, bounded batch, root oversight
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Irreversible
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Residual Medium, because irreversibility cannot be fully mitigated

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A lifecycle rule deletes data
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Policy scan failing deployment, runtime assertion, backup
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Irreversible
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Residual Medium

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Scheduled analytics become worker surveillance
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Measurement register, prohibited-use enforcement, DEC-SCHED-009
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Severe reputational and legal
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Residual Medium, because policy must close the residual gap

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Cross-tenant leakage in a batch occurrence
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Enforced anonymisation invariant, per-row scope assertion
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Severe
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Residual Low

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Operational burden exceeds the team's capacity
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded durable-workflow set, mechanism minimalism, DEC-SCHED-010
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: High
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Residual Medium

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Vendor lock-in prevents customer-hosted deployment
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Five adapter contracts, dual implementations
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: High commercially
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Residual Low

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Open decisions are treated as settled
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The closing statement of the chapter and AC-SCHED-380
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: High — a false completeness claim
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Residual Low
